_readme: Tier definitions and the committed error ceilings for the pyright
typing_baseline.py reads this file; CI runs it once per tier.
A measurement is only meaningful in the environment it was taken in:
'pyright_version' and 'environment' below say which, and the script
refuses to compare against a ceiling measured with a different
pyright.  Bump the pin in pyproject.toml's [ci] extra and these
Ceilings are per top-level package so that a regression in one
cannot be masked by an improvement in another.  Lower one whenever
the measured count drops; the script prints the slack it sees.
environment: pip install -e '.[ci]' on Python 3.12 with jax==0.10.2; no usd-core, pyvista, pygfx, rendercanvas, scikit-image, PyGObject or cupy
measured: 2026-09-20, branch feat/pep561-phase2; `surrogates` re-measured 2026-09-21 on typing/pep589-typed-dicts (58 -> 55: `TrainMetrics` makes `val_loss` a required key, so the three `metrics.get("val_loss") < float` comparisons in callbacks.py are no longer Optional); the interpreter moved 3.11 -> 3.12 on 2026-09-21 with the `requires-python` floor (chore/python-312-floor) and moved nothing: the typecheck job re-measured 0 in tier 1 and 61 / 55 / 1 / 45 in tier 2, every package exactly at its ceiling, on the same pyright 1.1.414

tier1.description: Annotated to zero: the packages refactors move through.

tier2.description: Public signatures annotated; bodies ratcheted only. These sit on untyped or optional third-party libraries (matplotlib, pxr, pygfx, pyvista, equinox), so the errors are overwhelmingly attribute access against something with no stubs.
